disease_label_per_paper: Pulmonary embolism presenting with itinerant pleuritic chest pain and migratory pleural effusion
presentation_summary: 41-year-old woman presented with persistent left chest pain for 8 days, worse with deep inspiration, without hemoptysis or breathing difficulty.
Initial chest CT and ultrasound showed left pleural effusion; she was treated as double pneumonia with pleural effusion.
On transfer, temperature was 36.5 C, pulse 71/min, respiratory rate 15/min, blood pressure 118/85 mmHg, and room-air oxygen saturation 98%.

White blood cell count, liver function, kidney function, myocardial markers, BNP, blood gas analysis, echocardiography, and D-dimer were unremarkable; D-dimer was 0.02 mg/L initially and 0.08 mg/L later.
After left chest pain improved, more severe right chest pain emerged and CT showed right pleural effusion.
CTPA 5 days after admission unexpectedly showed pulmonary embolism in the right pulmonary artery; no filling defects were seen in bilateral lower limb veins.

outcome.source_text_value: The patient made a complete recovery; three months later lung perfusion scan and ultrasound were normal.

quality_warnings: This case is a post-initial-imaging PE test: CTPA and migratory pleural effusion are rankable, while final diagnosis and recovery after anticoagulation are non-ranking.
Normal D-dimer, normal oxygenation, absence of dyspnea, absence of hemoptysis, absent lower-limb DVT, and unremarkable echo are retained rather than deleted.
